title: Biodegradation of an oxidized low molecular weight polyethylene by a Rhodococcus strain isolated from the gut of Atlantic Salmon
projectDescription: The project aimed at determining the enzymatic machinery deployed by Rhodococcus sp. ASF-10 while growing on a substrate known to contain alkanes, ketones and a low molecular weight polyethylene.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Rhodococcus sp. ASF-10 was grown using a substrate known to contain alkanes, ketones and a low molecular weight polyethylene, as well as on sodium succinate. Planktonic cells were collected in mid-exponential phase. Cells were lysed, and proteins were precipitated overnight using 12.5% ice-cold TCA. Proteins were digested using the S-Trap™ mini spin column digestion protocol (ProtiFi, USA) according to manufacturers protocol, reducing with 20 mM DTT and alkylating with 40 mM IAA. Proteins were digested using a 1:25 (wt:wt) trypsin to protein ratio. Peptides were analyzed on a nanoLC-MS/MS system (Bruker) using DDA PASEF mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS raw files were processed using the FragPipe v21.1 for protein identification and label-free quantification (LFQ). MS and MS/MS spectra were searched against the complete proteome of Rhodococcus sp. ASF-10 (5538 sequences), supplemented with common contaminants (e.g., keratins, trypsin, and bovine serum albumin, 118 sequences). To estimate false discovery rates (FDRs), a decoy database consisting of reversed sequences of all protein entries was included (5656 sequences). The resulting protein library consisted of 11312 proteins. Trypsin was specified as the proteolytic enzyme, allowing one missed cleavage. Variable modifications included N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, deamidation of asparagine and glutamine residues, and pyro-glutamate formation at N-terminal glutamines, while carbamidomethylation of cysteines was set as a fixed modification
